title: Record S14's review round 1
message:
Record S14's review round 1

Two [P3] findings on MR !21, both fixed: a fleet slot whose rows are
still stored is held, so a settlement is never undone on another hull,
and the player save syncs its directory after the rename. The reviewer's
four probes are a test. With the ablation of the fixes and their
verification: the full suite, the live held-slot check with the builder
and economy gates, and the local CI matrix.

title: Describe held fleet slots and the durable player save in the documents
message:
Describe held fleet slots and the durable player save in the documents

The vessel system document says when a fleet slot is held and how it is
freed, and that a settlement's row is deleted only once the player file
that names it would survive a host crash. The player management document
describes the save's rename and directory sync, and the player guide's
staff section says what shippurge does on a held slot.

title: Test a fee payment and a freight acceptance whose COMMIT gets no reply
message:
Test a fee payment and a freight acceptance whose COMMIT gets no reply

The review of MR !21 probed four paths that no test ran, and all came
out right: a dock-fee payment whose COMMIT reply is lost (paid once),
one whose COMMIT never arrives (nothing taken, the fee still owed), one
that is committed with the database away for the read-back (the hull
remembers it, and the next payment undoes it and pays once), and a
freight acceptance in that last state (the next acceptance undoes it and
posts one bond). They are kept as a test.

title: Sync the player file's directory after the rename that installs it
message:
Sync the player file's directory after the rename that installs it

save_char_checked() synced the temporary file and renamed it over the
player file, but never synced the directory, so the rename was durable
only at the filesystem's next journal commit. A settlement's row is
deleted as soon as the save returns, and that delete is durable at once:
a host crash in the window brought back the old file, with the ship's
side committed and no row left to judge it by.

The directory is now synced after the rename. A failure is logged and
not returned: the new file is in place by then, and a caller that undoes
its work on FALSE would undo it against a file that holds the save.
Every caller of the checked save gets the same guarantee.

Review of MR !21, finding 2.

title: Hold the fleet slot of a hull whose rows are still stored
message:
Hold the fleet slot of a hull whose rows are still stored

A fleet slot can be empty in memory while its rows remain: boot could not
rebuild the hull and left her persistence, or a purge failed and its
caller freed the slot anyway (a sinking, a merchant rollback, a removed
owner's stowed hull, a spawn rollback). The next spawn took the lowest
such slot and wrote over her rows, and an open settlement of hers was
then undone on the stranger: goods in a hold that never traded them, or
a dock fee on an unowned hull. shippurge called the slot empty, so staff
could not clear it, and her captain's accounts waited for good.

vessel_delete_persistence() now marks the slot until a purge of it
commits, boot marks it where it gives up on a persisted hull, and a
spawn takes only a slot that vessel_slot_free() passes. shiplist shows a
held slot and counts it as in use; shippurge deletes its rows, the
settlement among them, and frees it. The mark is runtime only: every
boot reads the rows again.

Review of MR !21, finding 1.

title: Accept the hoisted colors with the speed order's output in the damage gate
message:
Accept the hoisted colors with the speed order's output in the damage gate

The tick that gets the hull under way after strikecolors can land before
the output of 'speed 1' is read, and the check looked for 'colors fly
again' only in what followed, so the gate failed on timing alone.

title: Settle at login through the insurance delivery, and keep two settlements
message:
Settle at login through the insurance delivery, and keep two settlements

The login reconcile moves from a line of its own in enter_player_game()
into vessel_deliver_pending_insurance(), which that function already
calls: no unit test runs the login path, and the coverage gate holds
changed lines of interpreter.c to their subsystem's floor. The
settlement tests now enter through the delivery.

Two cases from a read of the build, each needing a second fault:

A COMMIT that got no reply and could not be read back may still be on
its way. A reconcile that read no row forgot the settlement; when the
COMMIT landed, its undo changed a hold that no longer held the trade.
The hull now forgets a settlement only after a locking read of its row.

A hull that boot could not rebuild was taken for gone, and her
settlement was deleted with her manifest and fee left as they were. It
is now kept until she is loaded or purged.

Tests for both, and for what no test ran: a mob's trade, the manifest
refused inside another transaction, and a sale and a fee payment made
right after their gate undid an earlier settlement.

title: Play an unpaid settlement's undo in the economy gate
message:
Play an unpaid settlement's undo in the economy gate

After the economy session's trades, the gate plants a freight acceptance
as the server would leave it had it stopped before saving the captain's
bond: a taken contract and its settlement row, which his player file
does not name. His next login must delete the row and put the job back
on the board.

title: Settle vessel trades, freight bonds and dock fees in two phases
message:
Settle vessel trades, freight bonds and dock fees in two phases

A cargo trade, a freight acceptance and a dock-fee payment write the
ship's side to MariaDB and the captain's gold to the player file, with
nothing spanning the two. A vessel_settlements row (schema Phase 25) is
now written in the ship-side transaction and carries the undo; the
player file is saved with the row's id (VSet), and the row is deleted.
A row left behind is settled from that file at login and before the
ship's or the player's next account: deleted when the file names it,
undone otherwise. The table's unique keys hold a ship's and a player's
accounts while one is open.

An unanswered COMMIT is settled by reading the row back. When that
cannot be done, or an undo cannot be recorded, the settlement is taken
out of memory, the hull remembers it, and her manifest is not written
until a reconcile has settled it.

cargobuy, cargosell, contractaccept and dockfees pay settle this way;
contractdeliver and contractabandon wait for an open settlement.
DB-backed tests at each crash point, help, the system document and the
economy gate's checks. Work item #12.
